selection.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms, whose boundary is the adapter's torch.cuda.synchronize() after the single prefill forward (input_ids [1,256], use_cache=True, logits_to_keep=1) plus first argmax, all inside phase 'prefill'; decode (31 steps, separate group 3e293c00b1fb98fbe29f) is outside the metric. Measured facts: clean original baseline ttft_ms=25.684 (project.json); the separate execution_timeline diagnostic shows the prefill window contains 2144 GPU kernels with an active union of only 20.571ms (hardware kernel durations, not host-inflated), so roughly 5ms of every clean TTFT window is host dispatch, launch bubbles and sync latency rather than GPU execution; prefill dispatches ~500 Python module calls and ~1600 aten ops through eager PyTorch (python_runtime corroborates per-call host cost, e.g. 8096 linear dispatches across the 32 forwards). The prefill GEMMs (aten::linear, 16.40ms CUDA, 76% of prefill kernel time) already execute at ~120-140 bf16 TFLOPS on ampere (per-group launch configurations), so kernel-level GEMM tuning alone offers limited headroom, while ~1820 small elementwise/norm/rope/cache kernels plus eager dispatch form the structural overhead. Opportunity selected: replace the prefill-phase Qwen3ForCausalLM.forward boundary (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f, target 'model', phases=['prefill'], exactly 1 observed invocation, call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a with parents [project invoke]) with a lazy CUDA-graph policy: capture the real parent-context forward on an early actual invocation (warmup exists: warmup=2 before repeats=5), then replay in later invocations. Replay re-executes the identical kernel sequence reading the stable per-state input buffer, removing Python/module/aten dispatch from the TTFT critical path while returning the same last-position logits and an equivalent KV cache object for the untouched eager decode steps. This is a region candidate because every nested prefill call's execution is re-routed (graph replay does not re-run Python hooks) - the whole prefill bundle is explicitly replaced at this one coherent editable boundary, and all 3646 prefill-phase observed call IDs are listed as affected. Numerics: same kernels in the same order on the same data, so outputs are bit-identical to eager, satisfying logits_atol/rtol=0.02, require_exact_greedy_tokens and state semantics; decode remains eager so decode_tokens_per_second is preserved. Known implementation constraints carried as explicit unknowns: static graph-pool buffers alias across repeats (returned logits must be cloned and the KV cache re-wrapped per invocation, preserving cache/alias semantics per the binding contract), allocator/graph-pool interaction, and capture must occur inside the actual adapter invocation context so the accepted parent's work is captured.
selection.hypothesis: Host dispatch, not GPU execution, accounts for ~5.1ms of the 25.684ms clean TTFT (25.684ms wall vs 20.571ms prefill kernel union); capturing the prefill forward as a CUDA graph during a warmup invocation and replaying it in measured invocations will cut ttft_ms toward the dense GPU-execution floor of ~20.6-21.5ms (expected saving ~2.5-5ms, i.e. ~10-20%), with bit-identical tokens/logits and no decode_tokens_per_second regression. This is a hypothesis to be tested by the framework's paired repeats: if the clean eager path already keeps the GPU dense (host fully overlapped), the measured gain will be small and the follow-up lever becomes fusing the ~1820 elementwise/launch nodes and projection GEMMs inside the same region.

proposal.rationale: Objective is ttft_ms for the frozen interactive workload; the selected region (group e0861b46dbeeb562f67f) is the single Qwen3ForCausalLM prefill invocation (call 900c23e99c808d2c9bda215a, target 'model', phase 'prefill', signature input_ids [1,256] int64 + use_cache=True + logits_to_keep=1). Measured facts: original baseline ttft_ms=25.684299 while the prefill region's diagnostic CUDA time is 21485.5us (group inventory), leaving roughly 4.2ms of the first-token boundary as non-kernel wall; python_runtime shows the host dispatching every one of the region's 3646 observed calls per invocation (546 module __call__s, 253 aten::linear, 145 RMSNorm chains, RoPE elementwise), with module _call_impl cumulative ~1.03s over 32 forwards in the perturbed cProfile capture - i.e. the batch-1 prefill is host-submit dense and the GPU idles between the ~2.1k recorded kernels. No installed bundles exist (search.json installed_bundles=[]), so the parent at this boundary is the accepted parent. The candidate replaces the region boundary with a lazily captured single CUDA Graph of the unmodified parent forward: on the first real invocation (inside the evaluator's dispatch context, per binding-contract.md, so the accepted parent's actual work is captured) it runs 3 side-stream warmup parent forwards, then captures context['references'][call_id] into a CUDA Graph with a static input buffer; every subsequent invocation copies the current input_ids into the static buffer and replays the graph, then rebuilds a fresh DynamicCache bound to the replayed per-layer K/V tensors and returns a CausalLMOutputWithPast with cloned logits. Replay re-executes the full native kernel sequence of the parent on the current input each invocation (no precomputed outputs), removes per-op host dispatch from the first-token boundary, and reproduces the parent's own kernels bit-identically (same kernels, addresses and order), so exact greedy tokens and the 2% logits tolerance are preserved by construction rather than by re-tuning. Decode-phase invocations of the same physical module have different signatures ([1,1] input with an existing cache) and no observed prefill-region call id, so they keep the parent path: decode_tokens_per_second is untouched. This is a single-device task (communication not_applicable per resources.json), world_size=1, so no collective participation is affected. There is no inputs/previous-feedback.txt and no inputs/previous-candidate manifest, so this is the first attempt and no historical rationale needs revising. Route labels cuda_graph_captured / cuda_graph_replay / fallback:* are reported per call through context['record_route']; they are diagnostics, with acceptance resting on the framework's own output checks and native trace evidence that the replayed kernels constitute the returned logits and KV cache.
proposal.setup_work: One-time lazy setup inside the first candidate invocation (quality/warm path, not per-invocation): 3 warmup parent forwards on a side stream (allocator and cuBLAS workspace warm-up, outputs discarded), one CUDA Graph capture of the parent forward with a static [1,256] int64 input buffer, shape/dtype validation of the captured logits ([1,1,151936] bf16) and 36x2 K/V tensors ([1,8,256,128] bf16), then an immediate replay that produces that invocation's real output. Retained for the process lifetime after setup: static input (~2 KiB), static logits (~0.3 MiB), 72 static K/V tensors (~36 MiB total), and the CUDA Graph private pool holding the captured intermediates. Memory-scope effects: retained graph-pool blocks increase reserved memory and framework.lifecycle_peak_reserved_bytes; warm-run framework.peak_allocated_bytes can fall because prefill intermediates now allocate inside the graph pool, while lifecycle peaks (which include this preparation) can rise; none of these counter movements is a general physical-memory saving, and the graph pool may also hold non-PyTorch-driver allocations not visible to these counters. Setup cost lands in whichever run triggers the first invocation and is not hidden from any measurement boundary.
quality_risks: CUDA Graph capture can fail if any observer active during the first invocation performs a capture-illegal operation; this is caught, labeled fallback:setup_failure:<Exception>, and every call then uses the eager parent, so correctness is preserved at baseline speed.

Replay reproduces the parent's captured kernels deterministically (identical kernel sequence and addresses); residual risk is cuBLAS run-to-run nondeterminism, which would surface as a quality mismatch and is bounded by the existing logits tolerance and exact-greedy-token checks.

The fresh DynamicCache returned per invocation binds read-only views of the static K/V pool tensors; the observed decode parent only consumes them through out-of-place torch.cat growth and shape reads, so no in-place aliasing occurs. The logits are cloned per call so no output aliases the retained static buffers. The layout expectation (transformers 5.16.1 DynamicCache.layers with keys/values/dtype/device/is_initialized) is validated after capture with a mismatch routing to setup-failure fallback rather than silent corruption.

Signature deviations (positional args, non-[1,256] shapes, attention_mask/position_ids/cache kwargs, output flags) bypass the graph and run the parent eagerly under fallback:signature, preserving semantics for any unforeseen call shape.
A runtime failure during replay or cache reconstruction permanently demotes the site to the eager parent (fallback:runtime_failure), so a single transient error cannot corrupt later invocations.

Graph replay does not rerun Python hooks: the inner prefill sites listed in eliminated_calls execute as Python only during the one-time capture warm-up/capture passes and never during steady-state replays; their contribution to the output is carried by the native kernels inside the graph, which the framework observes independently of route labels.
